articles.body: Originally published by Codexlava: Read the full guide . Start with the shape of your product Choose Django for a complete web application with users, data and an admin your staff can use. Choose FastAPI for an API: the backend of a mobile app, a service other systems call, or a workload built around AI models and other APIs. Some products use both. Django: a complete toolkit Django includes an ORM and database migrations, user accounts and permissions, an admin interface, forms and templates. That makes it a practical choice for a portal, booking system or CRM where staff need to manage data from the start. Django overview — Django Software Foundation FastAPI: APIs from Python type hints FastAPI uses Python type hints to validate requests and generate interactive OpenAPI documentation.

articles.body: The Hidden Bug in Your AI-Generated Code You merge a pull request that an AI agent wrote. Tests pass. The linter is happy. A week later, a customer reports a race condition in production. This isn't hypothetical. AI agents generate code that looks correct but contains subtle defects that slip past standard review. The problem isn't that AI writes bad code. It's that AI writes plausible bad code that survives human review. Here's what to look for, and how to catch it before it ships. What You'll Learn The three most common bug patterns AI agents introduce A checklist you can run on every AI-generated PR Code that automates the detection of these defects The Three Silent Killers AI agents are great at producing code that compiles and passes tests.

articles.title: How we check every AI-generated room render before a user sees it
articles.excerpt: Image models are very good at restyling a room and quietly bad at leaving the room alone. Ask for a Japandi living room and you get beautiful furniture, and sometimes also: a window that moved, shrank…
articles.body: Image models are very good at restyling a room and quietly bad at leaving the room alone. Ask for a Japandi living room and you get beautiful furniture, and sometimes also: a window that moved, shrank, or appeared over a kitchen sink where the photo shows a solid wall; a closet door that came back as a curtain, a sliding screen, or plain wall; a sofa parked across the only archway; a new doorway at the frame edge, or a niche carved into a flat wall; a camera that slid sideways; or the opposite: a picture that is almost exactly the photo you uploaded. Our users put these images in property listings, where a staged photo may change the furniture but not the windows, walls or doors ( why that line exists ). So every render is checked automatically before anyone sees it.

articles.title: I built a handover board for the friend who was doing all the remembering
articles.excerpt: I built a handover board for the friend who was doing all the remembering This is a DEV Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge submission: Build for a Friend. Live app · GitHub · Agent tools When my friend c…
articles.body: I built a handover board for the friend who was doing all the remembering This is a DEV Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge submission: Build for a Friend . Live app · GitHub · Agent tools When my friend came home from hospital, the hard part was never the medication. It was that four people were helping, each of them believed they knew the schedule, and nobody could prove what had already been given. She was doing all of it from memory, at 3am, with a phone full of half-finished messages. So I built her one board instead of a family group chat. What it does You open a board for one person. You log doses, blood pressures, the note the physio left, the blood test someone needs to book. Each entry carries who owns it , so "somebody should do this" has nowhere to hide.

What began as autocomplete suggestions powered by machine learning has evolved into AI systems that reason about architecture, propose design patterns, and understand the strategic intent behind codebases. Today's AI co-architects represent a departure from simple code completion tools—they engage in dialogue with engineers, challenge assumptions, and contribute to system design at a level once reserved for senior architects. This evolution reflects both the maturation of large language models and a shift in how development teams think about tool-assisted engineering.

articles.title: 5 Excel chores worth automating with Python (and how to tell which ones aren't)
articles.excerpt: Most "Excel problems" I get asked about are not Excel problems. They are the same five boring steps someone does every Monday by hand. Here is how I decide whether a task is worth scripting, and the s…
articles.body: Most "Excel problems" I get asked about are not Excel problems. They are the same five boring steps someone does every Monday by hand. Here is how I decide whether a task is worth scripting, and the small Python patterns that cover most of them. 1. Count the clicks, not the rows A 200,000-row file that you open once a year does not need a script. A 40-row file that three people copy-paste into a master sheet every morning does. Rule of thumb: if the same manual sequence happens weekly and takes more than 10 minutes, a script pays for itself within a month. 2. The four patterns that cover ~80% of requests Merge: many files with the same columns into one sheet (glob + pandas.concat). Clean: trim spaces, unify dates, split "Seoul, Gangnam-gu" into two columns, drop duplicates.

articles.body: El equipo de control de vuelo de Artemis II, en la Sala Blanca de Control de Vuelo del centro de control de misiones del Centro Espacial Johnson de la NASA, en Houston, el 10 de abril de 2026, durante el amerizaje y la recuperación de la misión Artemis II. articles.body: OpenAI's answer to Muse arrived this week, and it looks a whole lot like Muse dressed up in a suit and tie. Dots is a business-first product - for now, at least - costing a minimum of $100 per month. And sure, you can make a cute little Dot character, just like you can make a cute little Muse character. But OpenAI's early marketing is all about how you can use it to do Business Things: launch websites, reschedule calls, build slide decks for board meetings. Muse, on the other hand, keeps reminding me to buy a jacket I looked at. This week on The Vergecast , we're talking about Dots and the current state of agentic assistants.
